scenes.text: If you ever hike through the desolate hills of the American West, you might stumble upon a massive, seventy-foot concrete arrow pointing into the wilderness.
In the 1920s, before GPS or radar, pilots flying the first-ever transcontinental mail routes were flying completely blind at night.
To keep them from crashing, the government built a giant trail of bright yellow concrete arrows across the entire country.
Pilots literally looked out their cockpit windows and followed this glowing yellow brick road from coast to coast.
